idea: AI agents need to spend money, but handing an agent a wallet key means one bug or prompt injection can drain everything, while approving every transaction by hand defeats the purpose of an agent. Agent Allowance Guard is a NEAR testnet smart contract that works like a bounded corporate card for agents: the owner creates an allowance with a spending cap, an expiry and a recipient allowlist. The agent can only pull funds inside that policy — every spend is checked on-chain before any transfer is scheduled, written to an append-only audit log and emitted as a NEP-297 event — and the owner can revoke instantly. NEAR makes this natural: predecessor-based caller identity authenticates the agent, the contract account itself is the vault, and subaccounts model owner/agent/payee roles. Verified live on testnet: an allowed 0.25 NEAR spend succeeded; over-cap and non-allowlisted spends were rejected on-chain.
